title: Changing local transform in `_process` freezes RigidBody2D after 4.7
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7 (latest version on steam)
- Non reproducible in 4.6 stable




### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable (7d41c59c4) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H (20 threads) - 15.63 GiB memory

### Issue description


In a 2D scene, I have some rigidbodies with a rectangular collision shape, contained between 4 world borders. The rigidbodies can collide with each others and the floor/walls. The rigidbodies can be dragged by the mouse thanks to a joint2d. In 4.6 this all works with no issue.

After moving to 4.7, the rigidbodies seem to freeze after standing still for a few moments. They can be dragged as they spawn and they collide/stack sensibly, but after a few seconds they can’t be dragged, and in case a body can be moved (due to a process i describe later), the others stacked on top of it will remain fixed there instead of falling. Disabling collision with the floor via code also does not cause the rigidbodies to fall. The debug collision markers appear/disappear correctly, but the bodies don’t react.

For some reason, dragging the game window itself unfreezes the rigidbodies . Bodies will fall to the floor, or fall through the floor if collisions had been disabled. Forces applied via the joint also seem to update all at once. However the bodies freeze again after a moment.

I have set the “can_sleep” property for all bodies to false. I also set the project wide sleep timer to 99999, but there has been no change in behaviour. Printing the “sleeping” property of the bodies, they all return “false”.

I have also set the “disable mode” property to keep active but there’s no change once again.

Reverting to 4.6 fixes all the unexpected bugs.

I have read the changelog and migration guide, I have not seen any change regarding 2D physics so I believe this to be a bug, but i’d welcome anyone who can give me more info.



I have attached a minimum project that contains just 4 walls, two rigid bodies and a joint that follows the mouse and can be used to drag the rigidbodies. The bugs can also be observed for example by disabling collisions with the floor from the editor, the bodies do not react, until the window is dragged at which point the bodies fall through the floor as expected. 


Thanks!

### Steps to reproduce

In the attached project, clicking and dragging on the rigid bodies should allow moving them and observing normal physics behaviour in version 4.6.

In 4.7, attempting the same should display the unexpected physics behaviour. It should also be possible to disable collisions to the floor via code/editor and observe how the rigidbodies don't fall until the window is updated by dragging it, as in the videos
